# Decisions

Short record of choices that are expensive to reverse or easy to accidentally undo.

---

## 1. One renderer. The calendar is generated by Python only.

**Decided:** August 2026
**Status:** Active

### What

`python/build.py` is the only thing that renders the calendar. There is no second
implementation, in any language.

The Next.js web app that lived in `src/` was removed from `main` and preserved on the
branch **`web-ui-parked`**.

### Why

The web app reimplemented the calendar from scratch — its own cell logic, its own
Important Dates builder, its own PDF renderer (`@react-pdf` alongside WeasyPrint). The
two implementations were never checked against each other, and they drifted:

| | Python | Web app |
|---|---|---|
| Important Dates entries from `all_events.csv` | 45 | 56 |
| `no_school` days built from the same 14 CSV rows | 14 | 20 |

The 20 was a real bug. The web app's type table mapped `grades_due` to `no_school`, so
five ordinary school days rendered as black "No School" cells — 2025-11-12, 2026-01-21,
2026-02-02, 2026-04-10 and 2026-06-10. Nothing caught it, because nothing compared the
two outputs.

The consolidation gap was smaller but the same shape: Python groups repeat events under
one heading (`10/23, 2/19, 4/23, 6/4  PTSA: Board Meeting`), the web app printed four
separate lines. The asterisk rules had drifted too.

Two renderers of one document will always drift. Only one of them is printed and sent
home with families, so the other is a liability with no upside.

### If a web UI comes back

It very likely will — browser editing is genuinely useful for board members who won't
touch a CSV. When it does:

> **The web app edits `data/all_events.csv`. It does not render the calendar.**

Give it a preview if you like, but the artifact that gets printed comes from
`build.py`. The moment a second thing knows how to draw a day cell, this problem is back.

The parked branch is a reference for the UI work, not a starting point to merge — it
carries the duplicate renderer and an unauthenticated write API.

---

## 2. Unknown event types fail the build. The renderer never guesses.

**Decided:** August 2026
**Status:** Active

### What

Every event type is declared once, in the registry in `python/calendar_gen/event_types.py`. A type in
the CSV that isn't in the registry is a **validation error naming the row** — not a
default, not a silent skip.

### Why

This is the class of bug that produced the black school days above. The old code did:

```python
TYPE_NORMALIZATION.get(raw_type, raw_type)     # Python: silently passes through
TYPE_NORMALIZATION[normalized] || null          # TypeScript: silently guessed no_school
```

Both were guesses. One was wrong in a way that misinformed families.

### What this does *not* mean

The renderer has no opinion about **which** dates belong on the calendar. If a row is in
the CSV, it appears. That's the author's call, not the tool's.

The registry only declares **how** each type is drawn. To put a new kind of date on the
calendar, add it to the registry and say what it looks like — a one-line change, and now
it's a deliberate choice rather than an accident of what some lookup happened to return.

Types that should be listed in Important Dates but shouldn't change how the school day
looks use `mark = None` — see `informational` in the registry, which is what `grades_due`
uses.
